title: HIL bench descriptor
description: One descriptor per physical bench, authored by that bench's owner. `capabilities` is what routes a test run to this bench; `hardware` records what physically provides each capability, so swapping an emulator never changes what tests ask for. `expect` is the probe-verifiable half -- `tools/bench.py verify` diffs it against the live bench.

schema_version.description: Bumped only on a breaking change to this schema.

id.description: Fleet-unique id, e.g. bench-01. Also the concurrency-group key, so a typo silently disables this bench's queue lock.

owner.description: Who keeps this bench running. With several benches, uptime needs a named owner rather than defaulting to whoever built it.

board_rev.description: Backplane revision, e.g. BACKPLANE_HIL-A. Different revisions may move addresses.

location.description: Human hint for whoever has to walk to it.

hosts.description: SSH targets. The single source of truth for bench addresses -- nothing else in the repo should carry one.

runner.description: GitHub self-hosted runner identity. `tools/bench.py labels` emits base + capability labels; CI checks the runner actually carries them.

capabilities.description: What this bench can DO. These become runner labels and are what a dispatch matches on. Named for the capability, never the hardware -- replacing an emulator must not change what a test asks for.

hardware.description: What physically provides each capability. Documentation and debugging only -- never routed on. Answers 'which benches have a Pico?' without coupling tests to the answer.

can.description: CAN buses by role. Kernel netdev names are inverted vs the PCB silk (invariant #3), so the dev name is recorded per bench rather than assumed.

sample_point.description: Recorded because hil-can-up defaults to 0.875 while the AMS/ACU bus needs 0.6875; a mismatch bus-offs the DUT. Preflight asserts the live value.

slots.description: MLC carrier slot occupancy, keyed by slot number 1..4.

dut.description: Canonical DUT names. 'ecu' is the ECU08 target (historically 'vcu'); 'udv' is the microDV.

ina.description: INA226 address monitoring this slot's carrier current.

routing.description: Bench-physical wiring that tests must not hardcode. A test asks the descriptor for pack_current, never for DAC 3 channel 0.

expect.description: The probe-verifiable half. `tools/bench.py describe` drafts it from a live bench; `verify` re-probes and diffs. A bench that claims a capability it cannot demonstrate fails preflight in seconds instead of producing a puzzling red suite an hour later.
